issue.title: Migrate remaining mock-backed E2E specs onto the local provider; retire orphaned testMockData branches
issue.description:
**Finish what LIN-378 started.** LIN-378 (PRs #389/#391, merged) landed the reusable local-provider test harness (`tests/fixtures/local-harness.js`: `seedLocalWorkspace`, `localSeedFromLinearFixture`, `swimLocalSeed`, custom seeds + session `features` via POST `/test/set-local-session`) and migrated the surfaces it named: dashboard, swim (lanes/flow/vertical), ship (+ orientation), interactions/detail. The long tail of specs still rides the `NODE_ENV==='test' && accessToken==='test-token'` mock (`testMockData`), which keeps the mock branches in `server.js`, `routes/pipeline.js`, `routes/proxy.js`, and `routes/workspace-api.js` load-bearing.

## Scope

- [ ] Migrate every remaining spec that calls `/test/set-session` and whose surface the local provider fully models onto `seedLocalWorkspace` (custom seeds where assertions need specific data). Candidates include: search, swipe, error-handling, workspace / workspace-model / workspace-features, feature-toggles, settings, prompts / prompts-page / custom-prompts, brief, recap, recommend/streaming, roadmap, audit, foreman, periodicals, pipeline / pipeline-scenarios, dispatch-page, free-tier, landing-swim / landing-swipe. Some of these mock OpenRouter as well — that AI mocking stays; only the Linear-data mock migrates.
- [ ] As each `testMockData` site is orphaned (no spec depends on it), delete the dead branch at that site — per-site, incrementally, same gating rule as LIN-378.
- [ ] Retire `tests/fixtures/mock-data.js` / the `swimSample` session flag where they become unused — EXCEPT the visual-regression specs (`tests/visual/*`), which stay pinned to the mock fixtures so committed reference screenshots remain byte-stable.

## Boundary (unchanged from LIN-378, documented in the harness header)

Do NOT migrate: OAuth/PAT auth bootstrap (auth, pat-auth, openrouter-auth), the Linear API proxy contract (proxy, proxy-toggle-copy), cycle/team/estimate-driven flows the local provider declares off, and `tests/visual/*`.

## Notes

* Specs run with `workers: 1` (sequential), so the shared `local-workspace` store partition is safe — re-seed per test via `beforeEach`.
* Where a surface turns out NOT to be fully modeled by the local provider (e.g. needs cycles), leave the spec on `test-token` and extend the boundary list in the harness header instead of forcing it.
* Foreign-schema validation of the abstraction (subtasks/estimates absent, repos-not-teams) is deliberately NOT this ticket — it lands with the GitHub/Jira provider epics (LIN-178 / LIN-275).

## Relationships

Follow-on to **LIN-378** (uses its harness); the test-simplification remainder noted when closing epic **LIN-174**.

* **Tracked contract gap:** the only gap (free-tier harness fields) is **already closed upstream by LIN-405** — no route-around, no new gap ticket. The ticket's "close it here" instruction is satisfied by consuming existing code. Default-to-closing-the-gap is moot.

Re-point `data-id="proj-alpha/beta"` selectors to the seeded ids (or seed those exact ids). Medium effort. |

* `server.js` dashboard branch (S4/LIN-390), `pipeline.js` (S1/LIN-387), `workspace-api` block (S2/LIN-388), proxy contract, `tests/visual/*`.

* **Shared session route:** every in-scope spec uses the *same* `/test/set-session` → being replaced by the *same* `seedLocalWorkspace`. No two surfaces share mutable seed state because `beforeEach` reseeds and `localStore.clear(LOCAL_WORKSPACE_URL_KEY)` runs per call (`routes/test.js:437`).

* `feature-toggles` **↔** `settings` share the feature-flag interface (`features` object) — both now thread it through the POST body's `features` field (validated against the same whitelist, `routes/test.js:429-435`).

```
Independent, do in any order (low→high effort):
  settings ─┐
  workspace-features ─┤
  landing-swim ─┤      (each its own PR)
  landing-swipe ─┤
  feature-toggles ─┤
  dispatch-page ─┤
  free-tier ─┘   (consumes LIN-405 fields; no harness change)

  search   (independent; needs bespoke seed)

Within-file arrow:
  swipe: [Swipe Page] + [Swipe Dispatched Sessions]
            └──▶ unblocks [Recap UI — Swipe] + [Brief UI — Swipe]
                 (relocated blocks pinned ONLY because swipe was unmigrated)

Boundary (do alongside or last; each updates the harness header boundary list):
  error-handling (migrate 4 / pin 5)
  workspace      (migrate 3 / pin 7)
  foreman        (pin entire file)

Cross-ticket arrow:
  LIN-389 (this) ──blocks──▶ LIN-390 (S4): finalize boundary list + delete server.js mock
```

The **harness header boundary list** (`tests/fixtures/local-harness.js:17-44` doc-comment) must be updated to record the newly-pinned cases: foreman (proxy/foreman-prompt API contract), error-handling Team-Filtering+OAuth, workspace multi-workspace switch/remove/limit, and `dispatch.spec` (Dispatch API contract). It already lists swipe recap/brief, free-tier, feature-toggles, foreman as workspace-api mock consumers — those entries get updated/removed as their surfaces migrate.

## High-churn note

`routes/test.js`, `tests/fixtures/local-harness.js`, and the workspace-api specs are **high-churn** (10+ commits since 2026-06-10: LIN-356/377/378/387/402/403/404/405/408/413). Recent changes were protecting against: (a) the `test-token` mock short-circuit leaking into migrated specs (LIN-378's genuine-second-provider design); (b) cross-workspace counter bleed (LIN-405 made clear/usage routes `?urlKey`-scoped); (c) orphaned mock-branch deletion ordering (LIN-413 — a mock branch may only be deleted once ALL its test-token consumers migrate). Implication for S3: do **not** delete any `workspace-api`/`server.js` mock branch here (that's S2/S4); only re-point specs.

## Refactor-required check

**No blocking refactor required.** Every in-scope surface migrates by swapping the session-setup call and (for `search`/`swipe`) supplying a bespoke seed — the consumer seam (`seedLocalWorkspace` + `localSeedFromLinearFixture`) already exists and is consumed by ~20 specs. No new structural seam is demanded by this task; the one prerequisite (free-tier harness fields) is already merged (LIN-405). Refactor stays inline / N/A.

## Session-fit answer (explicit)

**NEEDS MULTIPLE SESSIONS.** This bundles 9 migratable surfaces + 2 boundary-split files + 1 pinned file + the boundary-list doc update. The established cadence is one surface per PR (LIN-410/411/412), and reviewers gate per-surface. Recommended batching (each a focused PR, all independent except the swipe within-file arrow):

* **Batch A (trivial swaps):** settings, workspace-features, landing-swim, landing-swipe.
* **Batch B (flag/queue UI):** feature-toggles, dispatch-page, free-tier.
* **Batch C (bespoke seed):** search.
* **Batch D (largest):** swipe (page + dispatched sessions → then recap/brief accordions).
* **Batch E (boundary + header):** error-handling split, workspace split, foreman pin, and the `tests/fixtures/local-harness.js` boundary-list update.

A single session could land Batch A+B if scoped tightly, but the full S3 surface set does not fit one session at the review granularity this repo uses.

Root cause: the committed fixtures were frozen **incompletely** in [LIN-587](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-587/evals-prefer-committed-real-task-fixtures-over-synthetic-stand-ins) — the task `state` was reset to `started`, but the real comment trails were NOT trimmed, so they still carry completion evidence ("PR merged / CI green / approved / closed"). A `started` task whose trail says it is done correctly routes to `review`, so every target collapses to the same answer. The fixtures were made *current*, not *accurate to a decision moment*.

This is NOT a system/engine regression — the routing eval (`eval-research-routing.mjs`) shows the engine routes across the full action space correctly. It is a fixture-freezing flaw, isolated to this one eval.

## Impact (blocking)

Until fixed, the recommend-baseline cannot give an accurate read on how well the engine chooses the next action. That measurement gates downstream engine-improvement work — so treat this as the blocking prerequisite: a full stop on next-action tuning until the eval can discriminate.

## Goal

Re-freeze the real descent targets at **key historical in-progress moments** so the eval exercises a broad range of next-action decisions, then grade them. We can re-use the same task multiple times to get a good array of fixtures.

The real tasks' comment trails already contain the full arc (research → plan → implement → review → merge as separate comments). Trim each target's trail (description, comments, etc) to a chosen decision point — the same red-moment technique `build-routing-fixtures.mjs` already uses — so the leaf sits at a genuine in-progress moment with a known-correct next action. Choose freeze points to cover a spread, e.g.:

* nothing done yet → expect `research` / (never `implement` before research or planning)
* research done, before plan → expect `plan`
* multi-session plan present → expect `breakdown`
* landed, not yet reviewed → expect `review`

Then add a per-target `expect` (acceptable next-action[s]) + role to each fixture, and score terminal-action accuracy + descent-correctness deterministically (mirror the `eval-research-routing.mjs` grader).

## Acceptance

* Recommend-baseline fixtures are frozen at trimmed historical decision points — `state` AND comment trail are mutually consistent, not current/closed state.
* Targets cover >=3 distinct expected next-actions (no all-`review` monoculture).
* The harness emits a scored summary (terminal-action accuracy + descent-correct rate), not just a capture table.
* Runs token-free on a fresh clone.

## Approach / patterns to copy

* Trim recipe: extend `scripts/eval/build-recommend-fixtures.mjs` with a per-target freeze-point/`keep` (like `build-routing-fixtures.mjs`).
* Grading: `scripts/eval-research-routing.mjs` (deterministic action grading + `expect` sidecar).

## References

[LIN-587](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-587/evals-prefer-committed-real-task-fixtures-over-synthetic-stand-ins) introduced the incomplete freeze (state reset, trail not trimmed). The routing eval is unaffected and correct. See the evidence + clarification comments below.

---

## Implementation Plan (LIN-596)

### Re-grounding / staleness check

Ticket references verified at HEAD. The two LIN-587 commits it describes (`3661258` fixtures-only harness, `bf0c494` routing eval) are present and the code matches the ticket's prose — `build-recommend-fixtures.mjs` still does `forceStarted` + a full, **untrimmed** `mapComments`, confirming the root cause. The 2026-06-22 committed baseline reproduces the monoculture: terminal action = `review` on 40/42 runs (only HAR-149 run3 and HAR-545 run2 = `implement`). No drift; the ticket is accurate.

### Surfaces the work touches (complete list)

1. `scripts/eval/build-recommend-fixtures.mjs` — add a per-target `keep` (trim recipe, ported from `build-routing-fixtures.mjs`) and per-target `expect` + `role`. Trim must be applied in `mapComments` (sort oldest-first, then `slice(0, keep)`) AND wherever the same node is emitted as a parent's `focusedChild`.
2. `scripts/eval-recommend-baseline.mjs` (the harness) — add a deterministic grader mirroring `scripts/eval-research-routing.mjs`: load each target's `expect`, compute **terminal-action accuracy** (terminal action ∈ expect) and **descent-correct rate** (descent reached the expected terminal id), and emit a scored summary in `table.md` / `run.json` (not just the capture table).
3. `scripts/eval/fixtures/recommend/*.json` — regenerated output (`harbour.json`, `linearviewer.json`); `synthetic.json` gains an explicit `expect: [review]` (its role string already encodes it).
4. Pattern source (read-only): `scripts/eval-research-routing.mjs` (`norm`, accept-set, summary rows) and `scripts/eval/build-routing-fixtures.mjs` (`keep` trim recipe).

Confirmed by searching the behaviour, not just the ticket: **no unit/E2E test references** `recommend-baseline`**,** `fixtures/recommend`**, or** `build-recommend-fixtures` — the fixture shape and harness output can change without coordinating a test rewrite.

### Freeze-point strategy (≥ 3 distinct next-actions)

A second, structural cause sits underneath the stated one: **all three chain targets per workspace descend to the SAME leaf** (HAR-149/545/616 → HAR-616; LIN-385/389/428 → LIN-428). So even with perfectly trimmed trails only **2 distinct leaves** are graded — trimming alone cannot reach ≥3 expected actions. The fix uses the ticket's own "re-use the same task multiple times" allowance: freeze the **same real leaf at several decision moments** as distinct targets (distinct bundle ids), picking freeze points from the committed full-trail fixtures (offline; HAR-616 has 9 comments, HAR-149 has 14, LIN-428 has 3):

* `keep=0` (nothing done yet) → expect `research` (never `implement` pre-research/plan)
* keep through the research recap, before a plan → expect `plan`
* keep through a multi-session plan comment → expect `breakdown`
* keep through the landed/CI-green recap, before approve/merge → expect `review`

Target design: grade `expect` on the **terminal/leaf** node; chain targets are graded on the leaf they reach. Keep graded targets short (leaf-only or 2-node) so the trimmed trail stays internally consistent.

### Cross-cutting concerns

* **Same node, two roles.** A leaf appears both as its own bundle and as its parent's `focusedChild`; both must use the **identical** trim, or the parent's context contradicts the child. → single shared trim seam in the build script.
* **Chain-wide trail consistency.** A coherent in-progress moment means the epic must not read "merged" while the leaf reads "nothing done". → prefer short graded targets, or freeze the whole chain at one arc-stage.
* **Descent guard interaction (LIN-353).** Descent is driven by `state=started` + a single open frontier, independent of trail content; terminal action depends on the trimmed trail. The two are orthogonal, so freezing a leaf at any decision moment leaves descent intact **as long as graded leaves stay** `started` (do not freeze a graded leaf into a terminal state).
* **Comment ordering.** Standardize on sort-ascending-then-`slice(0,keep)` so `keep` means "oldest N" consistently (the recommend builder already sorts; the routing builder slices raw).

### Strategy Framing

* **Cost of doing now:** extend one build script (trim + sidecar), add one grader to one harness, regenerate fixtures (read token), rerun baseline (OpenRouter key). Bounded and localized; freeze-point judgment is doable offline from the committed full trails.
* **Cost of not doing:** the recommend-baseline stays a `review` monoculture and silently green-lights any next-action regression. It is the **blocking prerequisite** for the LIN-431 next-action tuning family — a green-but-blind safety net is worse than none.
* **Cheaper strategy + its contract gap:** "just trim the trails, keep the two existing chains" is cheaper but **cannot satisfy acceptance** — two distinct leaves can yield at most two expected actions. Named gap: trimming fixes the homogeneous-input problem but not the structural single-leaf-per-chain problem; the reuse-as-multiple-targets approach is **necessary, not optional**.

### Scope Assessment — fits ONE session

Two code files + fixture regeneration, no test rewrites. Dependency arrow is sequential within the session: build-script change → regenerate fixtures (`PROXY_TOKEN`/`HARBOUR_PROXY_TOKEN`) → harness grader reads new `expect` → rerun baseline (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) → commit re-frozen fixtures + scored output. Single focused session.

### Open questions (carry into implementation)

1. Exact `keep` per freeze point — to be read off the committed trails (HAR-616/HAR-149/LIN-428) during implementation; some arcs may not cleanly separate research→plan→land.
2. Beyond `expect` + `role`, does any target need a `descentExpect` (expected terminal id) field, or is "terminal == last chain node" sufficient for descent-correctness?
3. Should the grader also surface a per-action breakdown (like routing's recall/over-fire rows), or just the two headline rates the acceptance asks for?

---

## Freeze-point resolution (LIN-596 — open questions closed)

Re-grounded at HEAD in a fresh session: `build-recommend-fixtures.mjs` `mapComments` sorts ascending but does **not** trim (root cause confirmed); `build-routing-fixtures.mjs` is the trim template (`sort` → `.slice(0, keep)`); routing grader uses the `expect`/`loop`/`avoid` sidecar; **no test pins** these surfaces. The 2 open `keep`/sequencing questions are now resolved from the committed full trails (read offline, token-free).

### Graded targets — leaf-only, reuse one real leaf at several moments (`keep` = oldest N comments)

Grade terminal action on the leaf. Keep graded targets **leaf-only** (no `focusedChild`, no children) so the trimmed trail is trivially self-consistent and stays `started`. Distinct bundle keys let one real leaf appear at multiple moments.

| bundle key | source leaf | keep | trail at freeze | expect |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `HAR-616@plan` | HAR-616 | 1 | [0] research finding only | `plan` |
| `HAR-616@breakdown` | HAR-616 | 2 | [0] research + [1] plan | `breakdown` |
| `HAR-616@review` | HAR-616 | 8 | through [7] blocker-resolved, before [8] review | `review` |
| `LIN-428@implement` | LIN-428 | 1 | [0] plan ready, before impl | `implement` |
| `LIN-428@review` | LIN-428 | 2 | [0] plan + [1] implemented/CI-green | `review` |

Distinct expected actions = **plan, breakdown, implement, review** = 4 (clears the ≥3 bar without needing a synthetic). Optional 5th: `HAR-616@research` at `keep=0` → expect `research`, **conditional on verifying HAR-616's description does not already state the pinned mechanism** (the research finding lives in comment [0], but the description is 5.7k chars — if it pre-seeds findings, also trim the description or drop this target; the bar is already met).

### Descent-correctness targets (keep the chains)

Keep `LIN-385→389→428` and `HAR-149→545→616` as descent targets, but trim every chain node's trail to a pre-landing moment (no merged/closed evidence) so the whole chain reads as one coherent in-progress arc. Suggested chain freeze: leaf at `keep=1` (HAR-616) / `keep=1` (LIN-428); epic/mid trimmed to before their close-out comments (HAR-149 keep≈11 pre-2026-06-14 close checkpoint; LIN-385 keep=1, LIN-389 keep=2 — before each `Closed`/`close-out` comment).

### Open questions — resolved

1. **Exact** `keep` — fixed above (read off committed trails HAR-616/LIN-428; chains noted). The one residual is the optional `keep=0` research target's description check.
2. `descentExpect`**?** — **Yes, add it** (optional per-target field = expected terminal identifier); default to the target's own `id` for leaf-only targets. `descent-correct = (terminal === (descentExpect ?? target.id))`. Cleaner than the "terminal == last chain node" heuristic and makes chain targets self-document their expected leaf.
3. **Per-action breakdown rows?** — Nice-to-have, not required. Emit the two headline rates (terminal-action accuracy, descent-correct rate) to satisfy acceptance; add per-action recall rows (mirroring routing's recall/over-fire) as an additive block if cheap.

### Same-leaf trim seam (cross-cutting)

Reused leaves get distinct bundle keys (`HAR-616@plan` …); the harness resolves `computeOne(id)` from `bundles[id]` and `target.id` must equal the key. Leaf-only targets emit no `focusedChild`, so the "node also appears as a parent's focusedChild" hazard does not arise within the graded set — only the descent chains carry `focusedChild`, and there the single shared trim seam must apply the identical `keep` to a node's own `comments` and to its copy inside the parent's `focusedChild`.

**Session-fit: still ONE session.** No new surfaces beyond the 3 already listed.

## Concrete evidence from LIN-587 (motivating this ticket)

The fresh fixtures-only baseline `scripts/eval/recommend-baseline/2026-06-22/` (K=6, committed) shows the monoculture: terminal action is `review` on **40/42 runs** across every target (HAR-149/545/616, LIN-385/389/428, FIX-448-leaf). Descent fires correctly through each chain — the gap is purely that the reconstructed-to-`started` fixtures (real tasks that have since merged, carrying landed/completion trails) all route to the same action, so the eval no longer discriminates routing quality and there is no per-target `expect` to grade against.

**Pattern to copy:** `scripts/eval-research-routing.mjs` (deterministic action grading + `expect`/`loop`/`avoid` sidecar). **Recipe to extend for fresh real in-progress targets:** `scripts/eval/build-recommend-fixtures.mjs` (text-free; already encodes the state overrides as code). Keep it token-free.

## Clarification — this is a MEASUREMENT gap, NOT a system regression

To avoid a misread of the title/description: the recommendation engine is **functional**. The `review` monoculture is an artifact of the fixtures, not the engine:

- The recommend-baseline targets are real tasks that have **since merged**; their frozen comment trails carry landed/completion evidence ("PR open, CI green, APPROVE, merged"). Given that input, recommending `review` is the **correct** action — the engine is right, the input is homogeneous.
- Independent proof the engine routes across the full action space: `eval-research-routing.mjs` shows 75–79% routing accuracy with research/plan/implement/blocked/bug/breakdown/review all firing on the appropriate cases (e.g. LIN-420→review, LIN-510→blocked, LIN-537→implement, SYN-21→bug). A regressed engine would route those to `review` too; it doesn't.

So this ticket is about restoring the eval's **discriminating power** (graded `expect` rubric + fresh real *in-progress* targets with varied next-actions), not fixing a broken engine. The degeneracy is also not new from the LIN-587 refactor — the targets had already closed and the pre-refactor harness built empty context against the flattened proxy, so it discriminated nothing either; LIN-587 just made the gap explicit.

## Planning complete — ready for implementation (one session)

**Root cause confirmed at HEAD** (not just trusted from the ticket): `build-recommend-fixtures.mjs` forces `started` but keeps the full untrimmed comment trail, so every leaf carries completion evidence and correctly routes to `review`. The committed 2026-06-22 baseline shows 40/42 `review`.

**Key finding the ticket didn't call out:** there's a *second*, structural cause. All three chain targets per workspace descend to the **same leaf** (…→HAR-616; …→LIN-428), so only **2 distinct leaves** are actually graded. Trimming trails alone can yield at most 2 expected actions — it cannot meet the ≥3 acceptance bar. The plan therefore leans on the ticket's "re-use the same task multiple times" allowance: freeze the same real leaf at several decision moments as distinct targets (research / plan / breakdown / review).

**Surfaces (3 + 1 read-only pattern):** extend `build-recommend-fixtures.mjs` (per-target `keep` trim + `expect`/`role`), add a deterministic grader to `eval-recommend-baseline.mjs` (terminal-action accuracy + descent-correct rate, mirroring `eval-research-routing.mjs`), regenerate `fixtures/recommend/*.json`. **No tests pin these** — shape change is safe.

**Cross-cutting notes:** (1) a leaf is emitted both as its own bundle and as its parent's `focusedChild` — both must use the identical trim (single shared seam); (2) descent (state=started + single frontier) is orthogonal to terminal action (trimmed trail), so graded leaves must stay `started`; (3) standardize on sort-ascending-then-slice for `keep`.

**Eval stays token-free on a fresh clone** (reads committed fixtures); only the regeneration recipe needs read tokens, and only the scoring run needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` — unchanged from today.

**Session-fit: ONE session.** Sequential arrow build-script → regen fixtures → grader → rerun baseline → commit. Full plan, surface list, cross-cutting check, Strategy Framing, and open questions appended to the description.

Open questions for implementation: exact `keep` per freeze point (read off the real trails); whether a `descentExpect` (expected terminal id) field is needed or "terminal == last chain node" suffices; whether to add per-action breakdown rows beyond the two headline rates.
